newsitem.title: UK: Jacques Vert says poor Q2 sales hit profits.
newsitem.headline: Jacques Vert says poor Q2 sales hit profits.

text.p: Women's fashion manufacturer and retailer Jacques Vert Plc said on Thursday poor retail sales in the second quarter of its current financial year had adversely affected profitability and cash performance in the first half.
Jacques Vert's shares fell steeply after the trading update and were 12-1/2 pence lower at 29p by 0712 GMT.
The group said a recovery in sales in the first quarter had not been maintained in the second quarter as sales of some Autumn/Winter ranges had been disappointing.
The retailer said it had continued to operate within its banking facilities, which run through to May 31, 1997. But it only expects to return to profit in the year to end April 1998.
In the year to April 27, 1996, it made a pretax loss of 5.038 million stg.
The company said it is closing non-performing stand-alone sites and concessions in line or ahead of schedule and within budgeted cost.
